title.zh: 卷372 列傳一百五十九 裕谦 谢朝恩 重祥 关天培 陈连升 祥福 江继芸 陈化成 海龄 葛雲飞 王锡朋 郑国鸿 朱贵
title.en: Volume 372 Biographies 159: Yu Qian, Xie Chaoen, Zhong Xiang, Guan Tianpei, Chen Liansheng, Xiang Fu, Jiang Jiyun, Chen Huacheng, Hai Ling, Ge Yunfei, Wang Xipeng, Zheng Guohong, Zhu Gui
title.raw: 卷372 列傳一百五十九 裕谦 谢朝恩 重祥 关天培 陈连升 祥福 江继芸 陈化成 海龄 葛雲飞 王锡朋 郑国鸿 朱贵

sentences.zh: =裕謙=裕謙，原名裕泰，字魯山，博羅忒氏，蒙古鑲黃旗人，一等誠勇公班第曾孫，綏遠城將軍巴祿孫。

translations.literal: Yu Qian — original name Yu Tai, courtesy name Lushan, of the Borot clan, a Mongol of the Bordered Yellow Banner, great-grandson of the first-rank Duke of Sincere Valor Bandi, grandson of Balu, General of Suoyuan City.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian, originally named Yu Tai, with the courtesy name Lushan, was of the Borot clan, a Mongol bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner, great-grandson of the first-rank Duke of Sincere Valor Bandi, and grandson of Balu, General of Suoyuan City.

sentences.zh: 父慶麟，京口副都統。

translations.literal: His father Qinglin was Deputy Commander at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qinglin served as Deputy Commander at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 裕謙，嘉慶二十二年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: Yu Qian passed the civil service examination in the twenty-second year of Jiaqing and was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian passed the metropolitan examination in the twenty-second year of the Jiaqing reign and was appointed a Hanlin Bachelor.

sentences.zh: 散館改禮部主事，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the Hanlin Academy he was made a Director in the Ministry of Rites and later promoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his Hanlin training he was appointed a Director in the Ministry of Rites, and was later promoted to Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 道光六年，出為湖北荊州知府，始改今名。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang he was sent out as Prefect of Jingzhou in Hubei and then adopted his present name.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Daoguang reign he was posted as Prefect of Jingzhou in Hubei, at which time he adopted his present name.

sentences.zh: 調武昌，歷荊宜施道、江蘇按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Wuchang and served successively as Circuit Intendant of Jing-Yi-Shi and Provincial Judicial Commissioner of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Wuchang and served in turn as Circuit Intendant of Jing-Yi-Shi and as Provincial Judicial Commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 十九年，就遷布政使，署巡撫，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was promoted in place to Provincial Treasurer, acted as Governor, and soon received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was promoted on the spot to Provincial Treasurer, served as acting Governor, and shortly thereafter received a substantive appointment.

sentences.zh: 二十年，英兵陷定海，伊里布奉命往剿，裕謙代署兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when British troops captured Dinghai, Yilibu was ordered to go suppress them, and Yu Qian acted as Governor-General of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, after British forces captured Dinghai, Yilibu was ordered to campaign against them, and Yu Qian served as acting Governor-General of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 時英艦遊奕海門外洋，江南戒嚴。

translations.literal: At that time British warships cruised the outer seas off Haimen, and Jiangnan was placed on full alert.
translations.idiomatic: At that time British warships patrolled the outer seas off Haimen, and Jiangnan was placed on full alert.

sentences.zh: 裕謙赴寶山、上海籌防，檄徐州鎮總兵王志元，佐提督陳化成防海口。

translations.literal: Yu Qian went to Baoshan and Shanghai to organize defenses, and issued orders to Wang Zhiyuan, Commander of Xuzhou Garrison, to assist Admiral Chen Huacheng in defending the estuary.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian went to Baoshan and Shanghai to organize the defenses, and ordered Wang Zhiyuan, Commander of the Xuzhou Garrison, to assist Admiral Chen Huacheng in defending the estuary.

sentences.zh: 疏陳規复定海之策，可無慮者四，難緩待者六，謂各省皆可言守，浙江必應議戰，且應速戰。

translations.literal: In a memorial he set forth a plan to recover Dinghai: four points that need not cause concern, and six difficulties that cannot be put off, saying that every province might speak of defense but Zhejiang must plan for war, and must fight quickly.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he outlined a plan to recover Dinghai, listing four points that gave no cause for worry and six difficulties that could not be deferred, arguing that while every province might speak only of defense, Zhejiang had to plan for war—and to fight at once.

sentences.zh: 又疏劾琦善五罪，略曰：「英人至天津，僅五船耳，琦善大張其事，遽稱：『畿疆、遼、瀋處處可虞，後來之艦尚多，勢將遍擾南北』。

translations.literal: He also memorialized impeaching Qishan on five counts, in brief: "When the English reached Tianjin there were only five ships, yet Qishan greatly exaggerated the affair and promptly declared: 'The capital region, Liaodong, and Shenyang are everywhere at risk; more ships are still coming and will soon ravage north and south alike.'"
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial impeaching Qishan on five counts, writing in part: "When the English reached Tianjin there were only five ships, yet Qishan grossly inflated the threat and at once declared, 'The capital region, Liaodong, and Shenyang are everywhere imperiled; more ships are still coming and will soon ravage both north and south.'"

sentences.zh: 冀聳聽聞，以掩其武備廢弛之咎。

translations.literal: He hoped to startle the court by sensational reports in order to cover his guilt for neglect of armaments.
translations.idiomatic: He hoped to alarm the court with sensational reports in order to conceal his guilt for having let military preparations lapse.

sentences.zh: 張皇欺飾，其罪一。

translations.literal: Inflating and deceiving — that was his first offense.
translations.idiomatic: Inflating threats and deceiving the throne—this was his first offense.

sentences.zh: 英酋回粵以來，驕桀日甚，琦善惟責兵將謝過，別未設籌，將士解體，軍心沮喪。

translations.literal: Since the English chieftain returned to Guangdong his arrogance grew daily, yet Qishan only blamed officers and men for apologies and made no other plans; officers and soldiers lost cohesion and army morale sank.
translations.idiomatic: Since the English leader returned to Guangdong his arrogance had grown daily, yet Qishan only blamed officers and men for offering apologies and made no other plans; the troops lost cohesion and army morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 彼軍乘敝，遂衄我師。

translations.literal: The enemy army took advantage of our weakness and thus routed our forces.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy took advantage of our weakness and routed our forces.

sentences.zh: 我船砲縱不如彼，兵數何啻十倍。

translations.literal: Even if our ships and cannon were inferior to theirs, our troop numbers were not merely ten times theirs.
translations.idiomatic: Even if our ships and guns were inferior to theirs, our numbers were far more than ten times theirs.

sentences.zh: 琦善不防後路，事敗委過前人。

translations.literal: Qishan did not guard the rear route; when affairs failed he shifted blame onto his predecessors.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan failed to secure the rear; when matters went wrong he shifted the blame onto his predecessors.

sentences.zh: 試思琦善未至粵時，未聞失機，其又何說？

translations.literal: Consider that before Qishan reached Guangdong no loss of opportunity was heard of — what then can be said?
translations.idiomatic: Recall that before Qishan reached Guangdong no missed opportunities were reported—what excuse remains?

sentences.zh: 弛備損威，其罪二。

translations.literal: Relaxing preparations and damaging prestige — that was his second offense.
translations.idiomatic: Relaxing preparations and damaging national prestige—this was his second offense.

sentences.zh: 沙角、大角砲台既失，自應迅駐虎門，乃其奏中不及剿堵事，惟以覆書​​緩兵為詞，且囑浙省勿進兵。

translations.literal: After the Sha Jiao and Da Jiao batteries were lost he ought swiftly to have stationed himself at Humen; yet in his memorial he said nothing of pursuing and blocking the enemy, using only reply letters to delay troops as his plea, and moreover instructed Zhejiang not to advance.
translations.idiomatic: After the Sha Jiao and Da Jiao batteries were lost he ought to have rushed to Humen, yet in his memorial he said nothing of pursuing or blocking the enemy, using only exchange of letters to stall the troops, and moreover instructed Zhejiang not to advance.

sentences.zh: 旋以給香港、即日通商定議，不俟交還定海後奏允奉行。

translations.literal: He then agreed to cede Hong Kong and open trade immediately, without waiting for Dinghai to be returned and the memorial approved before carrying it out.
translations.idiomatic: He then agreed to cede Hong Kong and open trade at once, without waiting for Dinghai to be returned and the throne to approve the memorial before implementing it.

sentences.zh: 違例擅權，其罪三。

translations.literal: Violating regulations and usurping authority — that was his third offense.
translations.idiomatic: Violating regulations and usurping authority—this was his third offense.

sentences.zh: 既畀香港換出定海，而英人仍欲通商寧波，銷售鴉片。

translations.literal: Having given Hong Kong in exchange for the recovery of Dinghai, the English still wished to trade at Ningbo and sell opium.
translations.idiomatic: Having surrendered Hong Kong in exchange for recovering Dinghai, the English still wished to trade at Ningbo and sell opium.

sentences.zh: 何以不在粵翦斷葛藤？

translations.literal: Why did he not cut off those entanglements in Guangdong?
translations.idiomatic: Why did he not sever those entanglements in Guangdong?

sentences.zh: 將就苟且，其罪四。

translations.literal: He was about to settle for a shabby compromise — that was his fourth offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was ready to settle for a shabby compromise—this was his fourth offense.

sentences.zh: 義律僅外商首領，向來呈牘，自稱遠商遠職。

translations.literal: Elliot was only the head of foreign merchants and in his memorials had always called himself a distant trader in a distant post.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot was merely the head of foreign merchants and in his memorials had always styled himself a distant trader holding a distant post.

sentences.zh: 上年在天津、浙江僭稱公使大臣，琦善不之詳，假以稱號。

translations.literal: Last year at Tianjin and in Zhejiang he presumptuously styled himself envoy plenipotentiary; Qishan did not investigate and lent him the title.
translations.idiomatic: The year before at Tianjin and in Zhejiang he had presumptuously styled himself envoy plenipotentiary; Qishan did not investigate and lent him the title.

sentences.zh: 失體招釁，其罪五。

translations.literal: Losing dignity and inviting provocation — that was his fifth offense.
translations.idiomatic: Losing dignity and inviting provocation—this was his fifth offense.

sentences.zh: 琦善已為英人藐玩，各國輕視，不宜久於其任。

translations.literal: Qishan has already been despised by the English and lightly regarded by all nations; he should not long remain in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan has already been despised by the English and held in contempt by other nations; he should not long remain in office.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，宣宗憤琦善受紿，斥伊里布附和，信裕謙忠直可恃。

translations.literal: When the memorial reached the throne, the Xuanzong Emperor was enraged that Qishan had been duped, rebuked Yilibu for echoing him, and trusted Yu Qian as loyal and upright and dependable.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, Emperor Xuanzong was enraged that Qishan had been duped, rebuked Yilibu for echoing him, and judged Yu Qian loyal, upright, and dependable.

sentences.zh: 二十一年春，罷伊里布，以裕謙代之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-first year Yilibu was dismissed and Yu Qian replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-first year Yilibu was dismissed and Yu Qian took his place.

sentences.zh: 裕謙至鎮海，英艦已去定海，渡海往治善後事宜。

translations.literal: Yu Qian reached Zhenhai; the British ships had already left Dinghai and crossed the sea to attend to post-battle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Qian reached Zhenhai the British fleet had already left Dinghai and crossed the strait to handle post-battle affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋實授兩江總督，以浙事付巡撫劉韻珂、提督餘步雲，自回江南部署防務。

translations.literal: Soon he received substantive appointment as Governor-General of the Two Jiangs, entrusted Zhejiang affairs to Governor Liu Yunke and Admiral Yu Buyun, and returned himself to Jiangnan to deploy defenses.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received substantive appointment as Governor-General of the Two Jiangs, left Zhejiang affairs to Governor Liu Yunke and Admiral Yu Buyun, and returned to Jiangnan to deploy the defenses.

sentences.zh: 初，英兵在定海，殘虐人民，既退，猶四出遊奕。

translations.literal: Earlier, when British troops were at Dinghai they cruelly abused the people; after they withdrew they still ranged about on raids.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while British troops held Dinghai they had cruelly abused the populace; even after they withdrew they still ranged about on raids.

sentences.zh: 裕謙捕獲兵目，剝皮抽筋而懸之，又掘敵屍焚於通衢。

translations.literal: Yu Qian captured enemy soldiers, flayed them and drew out their sinews and hung them up, and also dug up enemy corpses and burned them at a public thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian captured enemy soldiers, flayed them and drew out their sinews and hung them up, and also dug up enemy corpses and burned them in a public thoroughfare.

sentences.zh: 英人遂藉口復仇，大舉再犯浙洋，裕謙率江寧駐防及徐州鎮兵千，馳至鎮海督戰，令總兵葛雲飛、鄭國鴻、王錫朋率兵五千守定海，手緘密諭，付臨陣啟視，退者立斬。

translations.literal: The English then took revenge as their pretext and launched a major second invasion of Zhejiang waters; Yu Qian led a thousand men from the Jiangning garrison and Xuzhou garrison troops in haste to Zhenhai to direct the battle, ordered Brigade Generals Ge Yunfei, Zheng Guohong, and Wang Xipeng to lead five thousand troops to defend Dinghai, and personally sealed secret orders to be opened on the battlefield — retreaters were to be summarily executed.
translations.idiomatic: The English then used revenge as a pretext and launched a major second invasion of Zhejiang waters. Yu Qian led a thousand men from the Jiangning garrison and Xuzhou garrison troops in haste to Zhenhai to direct the fighting, ordered Brigade Generals Ge Yunfei, Zheng Guohong, and Wang Xipeng to lead five thousand troops to defend Dinghai, and personally sealed secret orders to be opened on the battlefield: anyone who retreated was to be summarily executed.

sentences.zh: 八月，敵艦二十九艘、兵三萬來攻，分三路並進，血戰六晝夜，三鎮並死之，定海陷。

translations.literal: In the eighth month twenty-nine enemy ships and thirty thousand troops came to attack, advancing by three routes at once; after six days and nights of bloody fighting the three commanders all died and Dinghai fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month twenty-nine enemy ships and thirty thousand troops attacked, advancing along three routes at once. After six days and nights of bloody fighting all three commanders were killed and Dinghai fell.

sentences.zh: 越數日，敵由蛟門島進犯鎮海，招寶山為要衝，餘步雲守之，別遣總兵謝朝恩守金雞嶺為犄角。

translations.literal: Several days later the enemy advanced from Jiaomen Island to attack Zhenhai; Zhaobao Hill was the strategic choke point, which Yu Buyun defended, while Brigade General Xie Chaoen was separately sent to defend Jinjiling as a flank position.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later the enemy advanced from Jiaomen Island to attack Zhenhai. Zhaobao Hill was the strategic choke point, defended by Yu Buyun, while Brigade General Xie Chaoen was separately posted to defend Jinjiling as a flank position.

sentences.zh: 裕謙疑步雲懷兩端，乃集將士祭關帝、天后，與眾約：「毋以退守為詞，離城一步；

translations.literal: Yu Qian suspected Yu Buyun of wavering and so gathered officers and soldiers to sacrifice to Guan Di and the Queen of Heaven, making this covenant with all: "Do not use retreat as your plea, nor step one pace from the city;"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian suspected Yu Buyun of wavering, so he gathered officers and soldiers to sacrifice to Guan Di and the Queen of Heaven and made this covenant with them all: "Do not plead retreat, nor step one pace from the city;"

sentences.zh: 亦毋以保全民命為詞，受洋人片紙。

translations.literal: "Nor use sparing the people's lives as your plea, nor accept a single slip of paper from the foreigners."
translations.idiomatic: "Nor plead that you are sparing the people's lives, nor accept a single slip of paper from the foreigners."

sentences.zh: 不用命者，明正典刑，幽遭神殛！

translations.literal: "Whoever disobeys — let the law punish him openly and the spirits destroy him in the dark!"
translations.idiomatic: "Whoever disobeys—let the law punish him in the open and the spirits destroy him in the dark!"

sentences.zh: 」步雲知其意，不預盟誓。

translations.literal: Yu Buyun understood his meaning and did not join the oath.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Buyun understood his intent and did not join the oath.

sentences.zh: 及戰，裕謙登城，手援枹鼓，步雲詣請遣外委陳志剛赴敵艦，暫示羈縻，裕謙不許。

translations.literal: When battle came Yu Qian mounted the wall and personally beat the war drum; Yu Buyun came to request that Sub-officer Chen Zhigang be sent to the enemy ships to show temporary restraint, but Yu Qian would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When battle came Yu Qian mounted the wall and personally beat the war drum. Yu Buyun came to request that Sub-officer Chen Zhigang be sent to the enemy ships to show temporary restraint, but Yu Qian would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 有頃，敵登招寶山，步云不戰而退。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy scaled Zhaobao Hill and Yu Buyun retreated without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy scaled Zhaobao Hill and Yu Buyun retreated without fighting.

sentences.zh: 敵復分兵攻金雞嶺，謝朝恩中砲殞，兩山同陷，鎮海守兵望風而潰。

translations.literal: The enemy again divided forces to attack Jinjiling; Xie Chaoen was struck by cannon fire and killed, both hills fell together, and the Zhenhai garrison troops fled at the sight of the wind.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy again divided their forces to attack Jinjiling. Xie Chaoen was struck by cannon fire and killed; both hills fell together, and the Zhenhai garrison troops broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 裕謙先誓必死，一日經學宮前，見泮池石鐫「流芳」二字，曰：「他日於此收吾屍也！

translations.literal: Yu Qian had earlier sworn he must die; one day passing before the Confucian school he saw a stone in the pool carved with the characters "Lasting Fame" and said: "Another day you will receive my corpse here!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian had earlier sworn he must die. One day, passing before the Confucian school, he saw a stone in the academy pool carved with the characters "Lasting Fame" and said, "Another day you will receive my corpse here!"

sentences.zh: 吾曾祖於乾隆二十一年八月殉難，今值道光二十一年八月，非佳兆。

translations.literal: "My great-grandfather died in martyrdom in the eighth month of the twenty-first year of Qianlong; now it is the eighth month of the twenty-first year of Daoguang — no good omen."
translations.idiomatic: "My great-grandfather died a martyr's death in the eighth month of the twenty-first year of Qianlong; now it is the eighth month of the twenty-first year of Daoguang—not a good omen."

sentences.zh: 」預檢硃批寄諭、奏稿送嘉興行館，處分家事甚悉。

translations.literal: He beforehand sorted out vermilion-rescripted imperial letters and memorial drafts and sent them to his lodge at Jiaxing, disposing of family affairs in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: He beforehand sorted out imperial letters bearing vermilion rescripts and memorial drafts and sent them to his lodge at Jiaxing, settling his family affairs in meticulous detail.

sentences.zh: 臨戰，揮幕客先去，曰：「勝，為我草露布；

translations.literal: On the eve of battle he sent his secretaries away first, saying: "If we win, draft the victory bulletin for me;"
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of battle he sent his secretaries away first, saying, "If we win, draft the victory bulletin for me;"

sentences.zh: 敗，則代辦後事。

translations.literal: "If we lose, then handle my affairs afterward."
translations.idiomatic: "If we lose, then handle my affairs afterward."

sentences.zh: 」至是果投泮​​池，副將豐伸泰等拯之出，輿至府城，昏憊不省人事。

translations.literal: When the moment came he indeed threw himself into the academy pool; Vice Commander Feng Shentai and others pulled him out and carried him in a litter to the prefectural city, where he lay insensible.
translations.idiomatic: When the moment came he indeed threw himself into the academy pool. Vice Commander Feng Shentai and others pulled him out and carried him in a litter to the prefectural city, where he lay insensible.

sentences.zh: 敵且至，以小舟載往餘姚，卒於途，遂至西興，劉韻珂等視其斂。

translations.literal: The enemy was about to arrive; they loaded him in a small boat and took him toward Yuyao, but he died on the way and was brought at last to Xixing, where Liu Yunke and others oversaw his encoffining.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy was about to arrive; they loaded him in a small boat and took him toward Yuyao, but he died on the way and was brought at last to Xixing, where Liu Yunke and others oversaw his encoffining.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太子太保，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，附祀京師昭忠祠，於鎮海建立專祠，諡靖節。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the combined hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry with one additional Junior Commandant of Cavalry, enshrined at the Capital Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, given a special shrine at Zhenhai, and granted the posthumous title Jingjie.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached the throne he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, awarded the combined hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry with one additional Junior Commandant of Cavalry, enshrined at the Capital Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, given a dedicated shrine at Zhenhai, and granted the posthumous title Jingjie.

sentences.zh: 柩至京，遣成郡王載銳奠醊。

translations.literal: When the coffin reached the capital Prince Zairui of the Cheng commandery was sent to offer libations.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin reached the capital, Prince Zairui of the Cheng commandery was sent to offer libations.

sentences.zh: 當初敗，餘步雲疏報鎮海大營先潰，裕謙不知所往。

translations.literal: At the first defeat Yu Buyun memorialized that the great camp at Zhenhai had broken first and that Yu Qian's whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: At the first defeat Yu Buyun memorialized that the great camp at Zhenhai had broken first and that Yu Qian's whereabouts were unknown.

sentences.zh: 韻珂等奏至，上始釋疑，予優恤。

translations.literal: When Yunke and others' memorial arrived the Emperor at last released his doubts and granted generous posthumous favors.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yunke and others' memorial arrived the Emperor at last released his doubts and granted generous posthumous favors.

sentences.zh: 幕客陳若木從兵間代裕謙妻草狀，詣闕訟冤，逮步雲論治伏法。

translations.literal: The secretary Chen Ruomu drafted a petition for Yu Qian's wife from amid the troops and went to the capital to plead injustice, leading to Yu Buyun being tried and executed.
translations.idiomatic: The secretary Chen Ruomu drafted a petition for Yu Qian's wife from amid the troops and went to the capital to plead injustice, leading to Yu Buyun being tried and executed.

sentences.zh: 嗣子德崚襲世職，以主事用，官至山東候補知府。

translations.literal: His heir De Ling inherited the hereditary rank, entered service as a Principal, and rose to Acting Prefect of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: His heir De Ling inherited the hereditary rank, entered service as a Principal, and rose to Acting Prefect of Shandong.

sentences.zh: =謝朝恩=謝朝恩，四川華陽人。

translations.literal: Xie Chaoen, a native of Huayang in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Chaoen was a native of Huayang in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 由行伍從將軍德楞泰剿教匪，積功至都司。

translations.literal: From the ranks he followed General Delengtai in suppressing the sect rebels and through accumulated merit rose to Colonel.
translations.idiomatic: From the ranks he followed General Delengtai in suppressing the sect rebels and through accumulated merit rose to Colonel.

sentences.zh: 累擢閩浙督標副將，從平台灣張丙亂。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Deputy Commander of the Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General's standard garrison and followed the suppression of Zhang Bing's rebellion at Pingtaiwan.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Deputy Commander of the Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General's standard garrison and took part in suppressing Zhang Bing's rebellion at Pingtaiwan.

sentences.zh: 道光十四年，擢狼山鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Daoguang he was promoted to Commander of Langshan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of the Daoguang reign he was promoted to Commander of Langshan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 從伊里布防鎮海，充翼長。

translations.literal: He followed Yilibu in defending Zhenhai and served as wing commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yilibu in defending Zhenhai and served as wing commander.

sentences.zh: 裕謙令守金雞嶺，力戰禦敵。

translations.literal: Yu Qian ordered him to defend Jinjiling and he fought the enemy with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian ordered him to defend Jinjiling, and he fought the enemy with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 敵別出一隊由沙蟹嶺繞出山後夾攻，遙見招寶山威遠城已為敵踞，兵遂潰。

translations.literal: The enemy sent another detachment around behind the hill via Shaxie Ridge to attack from the rear; from afar they saw that Weiyuan City on Zhaobao Hill had already been seized by the enemy and the troops then broke.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy sent another detachment around behind the hill via Shaxie Ridge to attack from the rear. From afar they saw that Weiyuan City on Zhaobao Hill had already been seized by the enemy, and the troops then broke.

sentences.zh: 朝恩扼砲台，中敵砲，墮海，屍不獲。

translations.literal: Chaoen held the battery but was struck by enemy cannon fire, fell into the sea, and his body was not recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen held the battery but was struck by enemy cannon fire, fell into the sea, and his body was not recovered.

sentences.zh: 浙人有親見其死者，歌詠傳其事，與葛雲飛等同稱四鎮雲。

translations.literal: People of Zhejiang who personally saw him die sang and spread the story, and together with Ge Yunfei and the others he was called one of the Four Garrison Clouds.
translations.idiomatic: People of Zhejiang who personally witnessed his death sang of it and spread the story, and together with Ge Yunfei and the others he was honored as one of the Four Garrison Clouds.

sentences.zh: 賜卹，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: Posthumous favors were granted and the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry was awarded.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous favors were granted and the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry was awarded.

sentences.zh: =重祥=重祥，張氏，漢軍正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Zhong Xiang, of the Zhang clan, a Han bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Xiang, of the Zhang clan, was a Han bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 世襲一等輕車都尉，金華協副將。

translations.literal: He inherited the first-rank hereditary rank of Light Chariot Commandant and served as Deputy Commander of the Jinhua Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the first-rank hereditary rank of Light Chariot Commandant and served as Deputy Commander of the Jinhua Brigade.

sentences.zh: 從葛雲飛戰定海受傷，复佐守金雞嶺，力戰死之。

translations.literal: He followed Ge Yunfei in fighting at Dinghai and was wounded, then again assisted in defending Jinjiling and died fighting with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Ge Yunfei in fighting at Dinghai and was wounded, then again assisted in defending Jinjiling and died fighting with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 處州營游擊托雲保，卞氏，亦漢軍旗人，偕重祥同殞於陣，並予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: Colonel Tuo Yunbao of the Chuzhou Brigade, of the Bian clan and also a Han bannerman, died in battle together with Zhong Xiang, and both were granted the hereditary rank of Junior Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Tuo Yunbao of the Chuzhou Brigade, of the Bian clan and also a Han bannerman, died in battle together with Zhong Xiang, and both were granted the hereditary rank of Junior Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: =關天培=關天培，字滋圃，江蘇山陽人。

translations.literal: Guan Tianpei, courtesy name Zipu, a native of Shanyang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Tianpei, with the courtesy name Zipu, was a native of Shanyang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 由行伍洊升太湖營水師副將。

translations.literal: From the ranks he was gradually promoted to Deputy Commander of the Taihu Garrison naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: From the ranks he was gradually promoted to Deputy Commander of the Taihu Garrison naval forces.

sentences.zh: 道光六年，初行海運，督護百四十餘艘抵天津，被優敘。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang, when sea transport was first instituted, he supervised more than 140 vessels to Tianjin and received special commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Daoguang reign, when sea transport was first instituted, he supervised more than 140 vessels to Tianjin and received special commendation.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢蘇松鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Commander of Susong Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to Commander of Susong Garrison.

sentences.zh: 十三年，署江南提督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he acted as Provincial Admiral of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he served as acting Provincial Admiral of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授廣東水師提督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Admiral of the Guangdong Naval Forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Admiral of the Guangdong Naval Forces.

sentences.zh: 時英吉利通商漸萌跋扈，兵船闌入內河，前提督李增階以疏防黜，天培代之。

translations.literal: At that time trade with England was gradually growing overbearing; warships intruded into the inner rivers, and the previous admiral Li Zengjie was dismissed for lax defense — Tianpei replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time trade with England was gradually growing overbearing; warships intruded into the inner rivers, and the previous admiral Li Zengjie was dismissed for lax defense—Tianpei replaced him.

sentences.zh: 至則親歷海洋阨塞，增修虎門、南山、橫檔諸砲台，鑄六千斤大砲四十座，請籌操練犒賞經費。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he personally toured the maritime passes and narrow places, added and repaired batteries at Humen, Nanshan, and Hengdang, cast forty great cannon of six thousand jin each, and requested funds for drill and reward expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival he personally toured the maritime passes and choke points, added and repaired batteries at Humen, Nanshan, and Hengdang, cast forty great cannon of six thousand jin each, and requested funds for drill and reward expenses.

sentences.zh: 十八年，英人馬他倫至澳門，託言稽察商務，投函不如製，天培卻之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Maitland of England reached Macau, claiming to inspect commercial affairs; his letter did not follow proper form and Tianpei rejected it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Maitland of England reached Macau, claiming to inspect commercial affairs; his letter did not follow proper form and Tianpei rejected it.

sentences.zh: 禁煙事起，偕總督鄧廷楨偵緝甚力。

translations.literal: When the prohibition of opium arose he joined Governor-General Deng Tingzhen in very vigorous investigation and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: When the prohibition of opium arose he joined Governor-General Deng Tingzhen in very vigorous investigation and seizure.

sentences.zh: 十九年，林則徐蒞廣東，檄天培勒躉船繳煙二萬餘箱焚之，於是嚴海防，橫檔山前海面較狹可扼，鑄巨鐵練橫系之二重，阻敵舟不能迳過，砲台乃得以伺擊。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Lin Zexu arrived in Guangdong and ordered Tianpei to compel the hulks to surrender more than twenty thousand chests of opium to be burned; thereafter coastal defenses were tightened — the sea surface before Hengdang Hill was relatively narrow and could be held, so huge iron chains were cast and stretched across in two layers to block enemy vessels from passing directly, and the batteries could then strike at will.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Lin Zexu arrived in Guangdong and ordered Tianpei to compel the hulks to surrender more than twenty thousand chests of opium to be burned. Thereafter coastal defenses were tightened: the sea surface before Hengdang Hill was relatively narrow and could be held, so huge iron chains were cast and stretched across in two layers to block enemy vessels from passing directly, allowing the batteries to strike at will.

sentences.zh: 則徐倚天培如左右手，常駐沙角，督本標及陽江、碣石兩鎮師船排日操練。

translations.literal: Lin relied on Tianpei as on his right and left hands, often staying at Sha Jiao and supervising the standard fleet and the Yangjiang and Jieshi garrison ships in daily drill by rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Lin relied on Tianpei as on his right and left hands, often staying at Sha Jiao and supervising the standard fleet and the Yangjiang and Jieshi garrison ships in daily drill by rotation.

sentences.zh: 七月，英艦突犯九龍山口，為參將賴恩爵擊退。

translations.literal: In the seventh month British ships suddenly attacked Jiulong Hill Pass and were repelled by Colonel Lai Enjue.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month British ships suddenly attacked Jiulong Hill Pass and were repelled by Colonel Lai Enjue.

sentences.zh: 九月，二艦至穿鼻洋，阻商船進口，挑戰。

translations.literal: In the ninth month two ships reached Chuanbi Bay, blocking merchant vessels from entering port and offering battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month two ships reached Chuanbi Bay, blocking merchant vessels from entering port and offering battle.

sentences.zh: 天培身立桅前，拔刀督陣，退者立斬。

translations.literal: Tianpei stood before the mast, drew his sword to direct the formation, and anyone who retreated was summarily executed.
translations.idiomatic: Tianpei stood before the mast, drew his sword to direct the formation, and anyone who retreated was summarily executed.

sentences.zh: 有擊中敵船一砲者，立予重賞，發砲破敵船頭鼻，敵紛紛落海，乃遁。

translations.literal: Whoever struck an enemy ship with one cannon shot was immediately given a heavy reward; cannon fire broke the enemy ship's bow, the enemy fell into the sea in confusion, and then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever struck an enemy ship with one cannon shot was immediately given a heavy reward. Cannon fire broke the enemy ship's bow, the enemy fell into the sea in confusion, and then fled.

sentences.zh: 敵艦久泊尖沙嘴，踞為巢穴。

translations.literal: Enemy ships long anchored at Jianshazui and made it their nest.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy ships had long anchored at Jianshazui and made it their nest.

sentences.zh: 迤北山梁曰官湧，俯視聚泊之所，攻擊最便，天培增砲駐營，敵屢乘隙來爭，不得逞。

translations.literal: The ridge to the north was called Guanyong, overlooking the place where they gathered; attack was most convenient there — Tianpei added cannon and stationed troops, and though the enemy often seized openings to contest it they could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The ridge to the north was called Guanyong, overlooking the place where they gathered; attack was most convenient there. Tianpei added cannon and stationed troops, and though the enemy often seized openings to contest it they could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 十月，敵以大艦正面來攻，小舟載兵從側乘潮撲岸，殲之於山岡；

translations.literal: In the tenth month the enemy attacked with large ships from the front while small boats carried troops to land on the flank with the tide; they were annihilated on the hill ridges;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the enemy attacked with large ships from the front while small boats carried troops to land on the flank with the tide; they were annihilated on the hill ridges.

sentences.zh: 复於迤東胡椒角窺伺，砲擊走之。

translations.literal: again they spied from Pepper Cape to the east and were driven off by cannon fire.
translations.idiomatic: Again they spied from Pepper Cape to the east and were driven off by cannon fire.

sentences.zh: 乃調集水陸兵守山梁，參將陳連升、賴恩爵、張斌，游擊伍通標、德連等為五路，合同進攻。

translations.literal: He then gathered land and naval troops to hold the ridge, with Colonel Chen Liansheng, Lai Enjue, and Zhang Bin, and Colonels Wu Tongbiao and De Lian and others forming five routes for a combined advance.
translations.idiomatic: He then gathered land and naval troops to hold the ridge, with Colonel Chen Liansheng, Lai Enjue, and Zhang Bin, and Colonels Wu Tongbiao and De Lian and others forming five routes for a combined advance.

sentences.zh: 敵乘夜來犯，五路大砲齊擊，敵舟自撞，燈火皆滅。

translations.literal: The enemy came to attack by night; the five routes' great cannon fired together, enemy ships collided with one another, and their lights all went out.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy came to attack by night; the five routes' great cannon fired together, enemy ships collided with one another, and their lights all went out.

sentences.zh: 侵曉瞭望，逃者過半，僅存十餘舟遠泊。

translations.literal: At dawn on inspection more than half had fled; only a little more than ten ships remained moored far off.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on inspection more than half had fled; only a little more than ten ships remained moored far off.

sentences.zh: 次日，復有二敵艦潛進，隨者十數，复諸路合擊，毀其頭船，遂散泊外洋。

translations.literal: The next day two more enemy ships slipped in with a dozen followers; all routes combined fire, destroyed the lead ship, and they then scattered to moor on the outer seas.
translations.idiomatic: The next day two more enemy ships slipped in with a dozen followers; all routes combined fire, destroyed the lead ship, and they then scattered to moor on the outer seas.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，詔嘉獎，賜號法福靈阿巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When victory was reported an edict praised and rewarded him, granting the title Fafulingabatulu.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported an edict praised and rewarded him, granting the title Fafulingabatulu.

sentences.zh: 二十年春，英艦雖不敢復進，猶招奸民​​分路載煙私售。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year, though British ships dared not advance again, they still recruited traitors to carry opium by separate routes for private sale.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twentieth year, though British ships dared not advance again, they still recruited traitors to carry opium by separate routes for private sale.

sentences.zh: 天培沿海搜捕，一日數起，复飭漁船蟹艇乘間焚毀敵舟，英人始改計他犯。

translations.literal: Tianpei searched along the coast and seized several cases in a single day, and also ordered fishing boats and crab skiffs to burn enemy ships when they found openings; the English then changed plans to attack elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Tianpei searched along the coast and made several seizures in a single day, and also ordered fishing boats and crab skiffs to burn enemy ships when they found openings; the English then changed plans to attack elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 及林則徐罷，琦善代之，一意主撫，至粵，先撤沿海防禦，僅留水師制兵三分之一，募勇盡散，而英人要索甚奢，久無定議，戰釁復起。

translations.literal: When Lin Zexu was dismissed Qishan replaced him, bent solely on appeasement; upon reaching Guangdong he first withdrew coastal defenses, leaving only one-third of the naval garrison troops, disbanded all hired braves, while English demands were very extravagant and for a long time no settlement was reached, and war broke out again.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Zexu was dismissed, Qishan replaced him and was bent solely on appeasement. Upon reaching Guangdong he first withdrew coastal defenses, leaving only one-third of the naval garrison troops and disbanding all hired braves, while English demands remained extravagant and no settlement was reached for a long time, and war broke out again.

sentences.zh: 十二月，英船攻虎門外沙角砲台，副將陳連升死之，大角砲台隨陷，並為敵踞，虎門危急。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month English ships attacked the Sha Jiao battery outside Humen; Vice Commander Chen Liansheng died, the Da Jiao battery soon fell, and both were seized by the enemy; Humen was in grave peril.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month English ships attacked the Sha Jiao battery outside Humen. Vice Commander Chen Liansheng was killed, the Da Jiao battery soon fell and was seized by the enemy, and Humen was in grave peril.

sentences.zh: 天培與總兵李廷鈺分守靖遠、威遠兩砲台，請援，琦善僅遣兵二百。

translations.literal: Tianpei and Brigade General Li Tingyu divided defense of the Jingyuan and Weiyuan batteries and requested reinforcements; Qishan sent only two hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Tianpei and Brigade General Li Tingyu divided the defense of the Jingyuan and Weiyuan batteries and requested reinforcements, but Qishan sent only two hundred men.

sentences.zh: 二十一年正月，敵進攻，守台兵僅數百，遣將慟哭請益師，無應者。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-first year the enemy pressed the attack; garrison troops on the batteries numbered only several hundred; generals wept and begged for more troops but none responded.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-first year the enemy pressed the attack. Garrison troops on the batteries numbered only a few hundred; generals wept and begged for reinforcements, but none came.

sentences.zh: 天培度眾寡不敵，乃決以死守，出私財餉將士，率游擊麥廷章晝夜督戰。

translations.literal: Tianpei judged that numbers could not match the enemy and resolved to die holding the post, paid troops from his private funds, and led Colonel Mai Tingzhang in day-and-night supervision of battle.
translations.idiomatic: Tianpei judged that his forces were too few to match the enemy and resolved to die holding the post. He paid the troops from his private funds and led Colonel Mai Tingzhang in day-and-night supervision of the fighting.

sentences.zh: 敵入三門口，衝斷椿練，奮擊甫退，南風大作，敵船大隊圍橫檔、永安兩砲台，遂陷。

translations.literal: The enemy entered Sanmen Pass, cut the chained barriers, and were driven back only after fierce fighting; then a south wind rose and a great fleet of enemy ships surrounded the Hengdang and Yong'an batteries, which then fell.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy entered Sanmen Pass and cut the chained barriers; fierce fighting drove them back only briefly. Then a south wind rose and a great fleet of enemy ships surrounded the Hengdang and Yong'an batteries, which then fell.

sentences.zh: 進攻虎門，自巳至酉，殺傷相當，而砲門透水不得發，敵自台後攢擊，身被數十創。

translations.literal: They pressed the attack on Humen from si to you hour; casualties were roughly equal, but the battery gates let in water and cannon could not fire; the enemy attacked from behind the batteries and he received several dozen wounds.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the attack on Humen from mid-morning until evening; casualties were roughly equal, but water seeped into the battery gates so the guns could not fire. The enemy attacked from behind the batteries and he received several dozen wounds.

sentences.zh: 事急，以印投僕孫長慶，令去，行未遠，回顧天培已殞絕於地，廷章亦同死，砲台遂陷。

translations.literal: As matters grew urgent he gave his seal to his servant Sun Changqing and told him to go; he had not gone far when he looked back and Tianpei had already fallen dead on the ground; Tingzhang also died together, and the battery fell.
translations.idiomatic: As matters grew urgent he gave his seal to his servant Sun Changqing and told him to go. Sun had not gone far when he looked back and Tianpei had already fallen dead on the ground. Tingzhang also died, and the battery fell.

sentences.zh: 長慶縋崖出，繳印於總督，復往尋天培屍，半體焦焉，負以出。

translations.literal: Changqing lowered himself down the cliff by rope, presented the seal to the governor, then went back to search for Tianpei's body — half the body was charred — and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing lowered himself down the cliff by rope, presented the seal to the governor, then went back to search for Tianpei's body. Half the body was charred; he carried it out.

sentences.zh: 優恤，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，諡忠節，入祀昭忠祠，建立專祠。

translations.literal: Generous posthumous favors were granted, the combined hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry with one additional Junior Commandant of Cavalry, posthumous title Zhongjie, enshrined at the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, and a special shrine established.
translations.idiomatic: Generous posthumous favors were granted, including the combined hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry with one additional Junior Commandant of Cavalry, the posthumous title Zhongjie, enshrinement at the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, and the establishment of a dedicated shrine.

sentences.zh: 母吳年逾八十，命地方官存問，給銀米以養餘年。

translations.literal: His mother Wu was over eighty; the throne ordered local officials to inquire after her and grant silver and grain to support her remaining years.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Wu was over eighty; the throne ordered local officials to inquire after her and grant silver and grain to support her remaining years.

sentences.zh: 子從龍襲世職，官安徽候補同知。

translations.literal: His son Conglong inherited the hereditary rank, entered service as an Associate Prefect of Anhui, and rose to Acting Prefect of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Conglong inherited the hereditary rank, entered service as an Associate Prefect of Anhui, and rose to Acting Prefect of Shandong.

sentences.zh: =陳連升=陳連升，湖北鶴峰人。

translations.literal: Chen Liansheng, a native of Hefeng in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Liansheng was a native of Hefeng in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 由行伍從征川、楚、陝教匪，湖南、廣東逆瑤，數有功。

translations.literal: From the ranks he campaigned in Sichuan, Hubei, and Shaanxi against the sect rebels and against the rebellious Yao in Hunan and Guangdong, with repeated merit.
translations.idiomatic: From the ranks he campaigned in Sichuan, Hubei, and Shaanxi against the sect rebels and against the rebellious Yao in Hunan and Guangdong, earning repeated merit.

sentences.zh: 累擢增城營參將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Colonel of the Zengcheng Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Colonel of the Zengcheng Garrison.

sentences.zh: 道光十九年，破英兵於官湧，擢三江協副將，調守沙角砲台。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Daoguang he defeated English troops at Guanyong and was promoted to Deputy Commander of the Sanjiang Brigade, then transferred to defend the Sha Jiao battery.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of the Daoguang reign he defeated English troops at Guanyong and was promoted to Deputy Commander of the Sanjiang Brigade, then transferred to defend the Sha Jiao battery.

sentences.zh: 及英艦來犯，連升率子武舉長鵬以兵六百當敵數千，發地雷扛砲斃敵數百，卒無援，歿於陣，長鵬赴水死。

translations.literal: When English ships came to attack Liansheng led his son Changpeng, a military licentiate, with six hundred troops against several thousand enemy; they fired land mines and cannon and killed several hundred enemy, but in the end there was no relief and he died in battle; Changpeng drowned.
translations.idiomatic: When English ships attacked, Liansheng led his son Changpeng, a military licentiate, with six hundred troops against several thousand enemy. They fired land mines and cannon and killed several hundred enemy, but in the end there was no relief and he died in battle; Changpeng drowned.

sentences.zh: 敵以連升戰最猛，臠其屍。

translations.literal: Because Liansheng had fought most fiercely the enemy dismembered his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liansheng had fought most fiercely, the enemy dismembered his corpse.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔嘉其父子忠孝兩全，入祀昭忠祠，並建專祠，加等依總兵例賜卹，予騎都尉世職，子展鵬襲，起鵬賜舉人。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported an edict praised father and son for fulfilling both loyalty and filial piety, enshrined them at the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness and built a special shrine, granted posthumous favors one grade higher according to the brigade general precedent, awarded the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry; son Zhanpeng inherited, and Qipeng was granted the rank of licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported an edict praised father and son for fulfilling both loyalty and filial piety, enshrined them at the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness and built a dedicated shrine, granted posthumous favors one grade higher according to the brigade general precedent, and awarded the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry. Son Zhanpeng inherited the rank, and Qipeng was granted the rank of licentiate.

sentences.zh: =祥福=祥福，瑪佳氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Xiang Fu, of the Maja clan, a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Fu, of the Maja clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 由親軍累擢冠軍使。

translations.literal: From the Imperial Bodyguard he was repeatedly promoted to Champion.
translations.idiomatic: From the Imperial Bodyguard he was repeatedly promoted to Champion.

sentences.zh: 出為湖南寶慶協副將。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Deputy Commander of the Baoxing Brigade in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Deputy Commander of the Baoxing Brigade in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 從提督羅思舉平江華瑤有功。

translations.literal: He followed Admiral Luo Siju in pacifying the Jianghua Yao with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Admiral Luo Siju in pacifying the Jianghua Yao with merit.

sentences.zh: 歷綏靖、寧夏、鎮筸諸鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He served successively as Commander of the Suijing, Ningxia, and Zhenbian garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Commander of the Suijing, Ningxia, and Zhenbian garrisons.

sentences.zh: 二十年，率本鎮兵援廣東。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he led his garrison troops to reinforce Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he led his garrison troops to reinforce Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，守烏湧砲台，與虎門同時陷，祥福死之，予騎都尉世職，祀昭忠祠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he defended the Wuyong battery; it fell together with Humen and Xiang Fu died, was awarded the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and enshrined at the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he defended the Wuyong battery. It fell together with Humen and Xiang Fu was killed. He was awarded the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry and enshrined at the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 尋詔與關天培同建專祠。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered a special shrine built together with Guan Tianpei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered a dedicated shrine built together with Guan Tianpei.

sentences.zh: 子喜瀛，襲世職。

translations.literal: His son Xiying inherited the hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiying inherited the hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 天培等皆以琦善不欲戰，無援，故敗，海內傷之，而福建總兵江繼芸又以顏伯燾促戰而亡。

translations.literal: Tianpei and the others all failed because Qishan did not wish to fight and gave no relief; the realm mourned them, while Fujian Brigade General Jiang Jiyun also died because Yan Bozhen urged battle.
translations.idiomatic: Tianpei and the others all failed because Qishan did not wish to fight and gave no relief, and the realm mourned them. Fujian Brigade General Jiang Jiyun also died because Yan Bozhen urged battle.

sentences.zh: =江繼芸=繼芸，福建平潭人。

translations.literal: Jiyun, a native of Pingtan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyun was a native of Pingtan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 由行伍拔補千總。

translations.literal: From the ranks he was selected and appointed Company Commander.
translations.idiomatic: From the ranks he was selected and appointed Company Commander.

sentences.zh: 道光六年，台灣張丙之亂，戰枋樹窩、小雞籠，以擒賊功擢守備。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang, during Zhang Bing's rebellion in Taiwan, he fought at Fangshuwo and Xiaojilong and through capturing rebels was promoted to Garrison Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Daoguang reign, during Zhang Bing's rebellion in Taiwan, he fought at Fangshuwo and Xiaojilong and was promoted to Garrison Commander for capturing rebels.

sentences.zh: 累遷台灣副將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Deputy Commander of Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Deputy Commander of Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 二十年，署南澳鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he acted as Commander of Nan'ao Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he served as acting Commander of Nan'ao Garrison.

sentences.zh: 總督鄧廷楨薦其才，尋擢海壇鎮總兵，調金​​門鎮，從顏伯燾守廈門。

translations.literal: Governor-General Deng Tingzhen recommended his talent; he was soon promoted to Commander of Haitan Garrison, transferred to Jinmen Garrison, and followed Yan Bozhen in defending Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Deng Tingzhen recommended his talent. He was soon promoted to Commander of Haitan Garrison, transferred to Jinmen Garrison, and followed Yan Bozhen in defending Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，廣東方議款，英艦遊奕閩洋。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Guangdong was negotiating peace while English ships cruised Fujian waters.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Guangdong was negotiating peace while English ships cruised Fujian waters.

sentences.zh: 伯燾素主戰，庀船砲備出擊，而新裁水勇未散，軍心不堅，繼芸以為言，伯燾不聽。

translations.literal: Bozhen had always favored war and prepared ships and cannon to strike out, but newly dismissed naval braves had not yet dispersed and army morale was unsteady; Jiyun spoke of this but Bozhen would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen had always favored war and prepared ships and cannon to strike out, but newly dismissed naval braves had not yet fully dispersed and army morale was unsteady. Jiyun spoke of this, but Bozhen would not listen.

sentences.zh: 七月，英艦泊鼓浪嶼，集水陸師禦諸嶼口，砲毀敵舟，而敵已撲砲台登岸，陸師先潰，繼芸急赴援，中砲落海死。

translations.literal: In the seventh month English ships anchored at Gulangyu; land and naval forces were gathered to defend the island passes, cannon destroyed enemy boats, but the enemy had already rushed the batteries and landed; the land force broke first; Jiyun hurried to reinforce, was struck by cannon fire, fell into the sea, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month English ships anchored at Gulangyu. Land and naval forces were gathered to defend the island passes and cannon destroyed enemy boats, but the enemy had already rushed the batteries and landed. The land force broke first. Jiyun hurried to reinforce, was struck by cannon fire, fell into the sea, and died.

sentences.zh: 護理延平協副將凌志、淮口都司王世俊同殉。

translations.literal: Acting Deputy Commander Ling Zhi of Yanping Brigade and Huai River Garrison Commander Wang Shijun died together as martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Deputy Commander Ling Zhi of the Yanping Brigade and Huai River Garrison Commander Wang Shijun died together as martyrs.

sentences.zh: 凌志，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Ling Zhi, of the Fuca clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Zhi, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: =陳化成=陳化成，字蓮峰，福建同安人。

translations.literal: Chen Huacheng, courtesy name Lianfeng, a native of Tong'an in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huacheng, with the courtesy name Lianfeng, was a native of Tong'an in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 由行伍授水師把總。

translations.literal: From the ranks he was appointed Petty Officer of the naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: From the ranks he was appointed Petty Officer of the naval forces.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，從提督李長庚擊蔡牽，數有功，以勇聞。

translations.literal: In the Jiaqing period he followed Admiral Li Changgeng in attacking Cai Qian with repeated merit and was famed for valor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiaqing reign he followed Admiral Li Changgeng in attacking Cai Qian with repeated merit and was famed for valor.

sentences.zh: 累擢烽火門參將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Colonel of Fenghuomen.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Colonel of Fenghuomen.

sentences.zh: 總督董教增薦其久歷閩、粵水師，手擒巨盜四百八十餘人，勤勞最著，請補澎湖副將，以籍隸本省，格不行。

translations.literal: Governor-General Dong Jiaozeng recommended that he had long served in Fujian and Guangdong naval forces, personally captured more than 480 major pirates, and his diligent service was most outstanding, requesting appointment as Deputy Commander of Penghu, but because his household register was in the same province the request was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Dong Jiaozeng recommended that he had long served in the Fujian and Guangdong naval forces, personally captured more than 480 major pirates, and his diligent service was most outstanding, requesting appointment as Deputy Commander of Penghu, but because his household register was in the same province the request was blocked.

sentences.zh: 遷瑞安協副將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Deputy Commander of the Ruian Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Deputy Commander of the Ruian Brigade.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，乃調澎湖。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was at last transferred to Penghu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Daoguang reign he was at last transferred to Penghu.

sentences.zh: 歷碣石、金門兩鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He served successively as Commander of Jieshi and Jinmen garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Commander of the Jieshi and Jinmen garrisons.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢福建水師提督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to Admiral of the Fujian Naval Forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to Admiral of the Fujian Naval Forces.

sentences.zh: 十二年，英吉利船駛入閩、浙、江南、山東洋面，命化成督師巡邏，以備不虞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year English ships entered the seas of Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangnan, and Shandong; Huacheng was ordered to command troops on patrol to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year English ships entered the seas of Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangnan, and Shandong. Huacheng was ordered to command troops on patrol to guard against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 同安潘塗、宦潯、柏頭諸鄉素為盜藪，掩捕悉平之。

translations.literal: The villages of Pantu, Huanxun, and Baitou in Tong'an had long been pirate dens; he raided and captured them all and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The villages of Pantu, Huanxun, and Baitou in Tong'an had long been pirate dens; he raided and captured them all and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 二十年，英艦犯閩，化成率師船擊之於梅林洋，尋退去。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year when English ships attacked Fujian Huacheng led the fleet to strike them at Meilin Bay and they soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, when English ships attacked Fujian, Huacheng led the fleet to strike them at Meilin Bay and they soon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 調江南提督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Provincial Admiral of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Provincial Admiral of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 江南水師素怯懦，化成選閩中親軍教練，士氣稍振。

translations.literal: The Jiangnan naval forces had long been timid; Huacheng selected personal troops from Fujian to train them and morale was somewhat revived.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan naval forces had long been timid. Huacheng selected personal troops from Fujian to train them, and morale was somewhat revived.

sentences.zh: 籌備吳淞防務，修台鑄砲，沿海塘築二十六堡。

translations.literal: He prepared defenses at Wusong, repaired batteries and cast cannon, and built twenty-six forts along the coastal dikes.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared the defenses at Wusong, repaired batteries and cast cannon, and built twenty-six forts along the coastal dikes.

sentences.zh: 化成枕戈海上凡二年，與士卒同勞苦，風雨寒暑不避，總督裕謙、牛鑑皆倚為長城。

translations.literal: Huacheng slept beside his weapons at sea for two years, sharing hardship with officers and soldiers, never avoiding wind, rain, cold, or heat; Governors-General Yu Qian and Niu Jian both relied on him as their great wall.
translations.idiomatic: Huacheng slept beside his weapons at sea for two years, sharing hardship with officers and soldiers and never avoiding wind, rain, cold, or heat. Governors-General Yu Qian and Niu Jian both relied on him as their great wall.

sentences.zh: 當定海三總兵戰歿，裕謙亦殉，化成哭之慟，謂所部曰：「武臣死於疆場，幸也。

translations.literal: When the three brigade generals at Dinghai died in battle and Yu Qian also died a martyr's death, Huacheng wept bitterly and told his troops: "For a military man to die on the battlefield is fortune."
translations.idiomatic: When the three brigade generals at Dinghai died in battle and Yu Qian also died a martyr's death, Huacheng wept bitterly and told his troops, "For a military man to die on the battlefield is fortune."

sentences.zh: 汝曹勉之！

translations.literal: "You must exert yourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: "You must exert yourselves!"

sentences.zh: 」吳淞口以東西砲台為犄角，化成率參將周世榮守西台，參將崔吉瑞、游擊董永清守東台，而徐州鎮王志元守小沙背，以防繞襲。

translations.literal: At Wusong the eastern and western batteries formed flank positions; Huacheng led Colonel Zhou Shirong to defend the western battery, Colonel Cui Jirui and Colonel Dong Yongqing the eastern battery, while Wang Zhiyuan of Xuzhou Garrison defended Xiaoshabei to guard against encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: At Wusong the eastern and western batteries formed flank positions. Huacheng led Colonel Zhou Shirong to defend the western battery, Colonel Cui Jirui and Colonel Dong Yongqing the eastern battery, while Wang Zhiyuan of the Xuzhou Garrison defended Xiaoshabei to guard against encirclement.

sentences.zh: 二十二年五月，敵來犯，泊外洋，以汽舟二，列木人兩舷，繞小沙背鄉西台，欲試我效力。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-second year the enemy came to attack and anchored in the outer seas; with two steam vessels they lined wooden figures along both sides, circled Xiaoshabei toward the western battery, wishing to test our effectiveness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twenty-second year the enemy came to attack and anchored in the outer seas. With two steam vessels they lined wooden figures along both sides and circled Xiaoshabei toward the western battery, wishing to test our effectiveness.

sentences.zh: 化成知之，不發，敵舟旋去，以水牌浮書約戰。

translations.literal: Huacheng knew it and did not fire; the enemy ships soon left and floated a written challenge on a board.
translations.idiomatic: Huacheng knew it and did not fire. The enemy ships soon left and floated a written challenge on a board.

sentences.zh: 牛鑑方駐寶山，慮敵鋒不可當。

translations.literal: Niu Jian was then stationed at Baoshan and feared the enemy's edge could not be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Jian was then stationed at Baoshan and feared the enemy's assault could not be withstood.

sentences.zh: 化成曰​​：「吾經歷海洋四十餘年，在砲彈中入死出生，難以數計。

translations.literal: Huacheng said: "I have spent more than forty years on the seas, passing between life and death amid cannonballs beyond counting."
translations.idiomatic: Huacheng said, "I have spent more than forty years on the seas, passing between life and death amid cannonballs beyond counting."

sentences.zh: 今見敵勿擊，是畏敵也。

translations.literal: "Now to see the enemy and not strike is to fear the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: "Now to see the enemy and not strike is to fear the enemy."

sentences.zh: 奉命討賊，有進無退。

translations.literal: "Ordered to suppress bandits, there is advance but no retreat."
translations.idiomatic: "Ordered to suppress the enemy, there is advance but no retreat."

sentences.zh: 扼險可勝，公勿怖！

translations.literal: "Hold the narrow passes and victory is possible; do not be afraid!"
translations.idiomatic: "Hold the narrow passes and victory is possible. Do not be afraid!"

sentences.zh: 」鑑乃以化成心如鐵石，士卒用命，民情固結入告，詔特嘉之。

translations.literal: Jian then reported that Huacheng's heart was like iron and stone, troops obeyed orders, and the people's loyalty was firm; an edict specially praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian then reported that Huacheng's heart was like iron and stone, the troops obeyed orders, and the people's loyalty was firm. An edict specially praised him.

sentences.zh: 越數日，敵艦銜尾進，化成麾旗發砲，毀敵艦三，殲斃甚眾。

translations.literal: Several days later enemy ships advanced in a line; Huacheng waved the flag and opened fire, destroying three enemy ships and killing very many.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later enemy ships advanced in a line. Huacheng waved the flag and opened fire, destroying three enemy ships and killing very many.

sentences.zh: 鑑聞師得力，親至校場督戰，敵以桅砲注擊，毀演武廳，鑑遽退。

translations.literal: When Jian heard the army was gaining advantage he came in person to the drill ground to direct battle; the enemy aimed mast-cannon fire and destroyed the drill hall; Jian hastily withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian heard the army was gaining advantage he came in person to the drill ground to direct the battle. The enemy aimed mast-cannon fire and destroyed the drill hall, and Jian hastily withdrew.

sentences.zh: 敵攻壞土塘，由小沙背登岸，徐州兵先奔，東台亦潰，萃攻西台，部將守備韋印福，千總錢金玉、許攀桂，外委徐大華等皆戰死。

translations.literal: The enemy breached the earthen dike and landed from Xiaoshabei; Xuzhou troops fled first, the eastern battery also broke, and all forces converged to attack the western battery; Garrison Commander Wei Yinfu, Company Commanders Qian Jinyu and Xu Pan'gui, and Sub-officer Xu Dahua all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy breached the earthen dike and landed from Xiaoshabei. Xuzhou troops fled first, the eastern battery also broke, and all forces converged to attack the western battery. Garrison Commander Wei Yinfu, Company Commanders Qian Jinyu and Xu Pan'gui, and Sub-officer Xu Dahua all died in battle.

sentences.zh: 屍積於前，化成猶掬子藥親發砲，俄中彈，噴血而殞。

translations.literal: Corpses piled before him yet Huacheng still scooped powder and fired cannon in person; soon he was struck and died spitting blood.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses piled before him, yet Huacheng still scooped powder and fired cannon in person. Soon he was struck and died spitting blood.

sentences.zh: 砲台既失，寶山、山海相繼陷。

translations.literal: Once the batteries were lost, Baoshan and Shanghai fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Once the batteries were lost, Baoshan and Shanghai fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 越八日，鄉民始負其屍出，殮於嘉定。

translations.literal: Eight days later the villagers at last carried his body out and encoffined him at Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: Eight days later the villagers at last carried his body out and encoffined him at Jiading.

sentences.zh: 事聞，宣宗震悼，特詔優恤，賜銀一千兩治喪，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，諡忠愍，於殉難處所及原籍並建專祠。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported the Xuanzong Emperor was deeply grieved; a special edict granted generous posthumous favors, one thousand taels of silver for the funeral, the combined hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry with one additional Junior Commandant of Cavalry, posthumous title Zhongmin, and special shrines at the place of martyrdom and his native place.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported Emperor Xuanzong was deeply grieved. A special edict granted generous posthumous favors, one thousand taels of silver for the funeral, the combined hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry with one additional Junior Commandant of Cavalry, the posthumous title Zhongmin, and dedicated shrines at the place of martyrdom and his native place.

sentences.zh: 子廷芳，襲世職；

translations.literal: His son Tingfang inherited the hereditary rank;
translations.idiomatic: His son Tingfang inherited the hereditary rank;

sentences.zh: 廷棻，賜舉人。

translations.literal: Tingfen was granted the rank of licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: Tingfen was granted the rank of licentiate.

sentences.zh: =海齡=海齡，郭洛羅氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Hai Ling, of the Guoluoluo clan, a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Hai Ling, of the Guoluoluo clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 由驍騎校授張家口守備。

translations.literal: From Bold Cavalry Colonel he was appointed Garrison Commander of Zhangjiakou.
translations.idiomatic: From Bold Cavalry Colonel he was appointed Garrison Commander of Zhangjiakou.

sentences.zh: 累擢大名、正定兩鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Commander of Daming and Zhengding garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Commander of the Daming and Zhengding garrisons.

sentences.zh: 以事降二等侍衛，充古城領隊大臣。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to Second-rank Imperial Bodyguard and served as Commandant of the Gucheng detachment.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was demoted to Second-rank Imperial Bodyguard and served as Commandant of the Gucheng detachment.

sentences.zh: 歷西安、江寧、京口副都統。

translations.literal: He served successively as Deputy Commander at Xi'an, Jiangning, and Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Deputy Commander at Xi'an, Jiangning, and Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 英兵既陷吳淞，由海入江，六月，犯鎮江，提督齊慎、劉承孝敗退，遂攻城，海齡率駐防兵死守二日，敵以雲梯入城屠旗、民，海齡與全家殉焉。

translations.literal: After English troops captured Wusong they entered the Yangzi by sea; in the sixth month they attacked Zhenjiang; Admiral Qi Shen and Liu Chengxiao were defeated and withdrew; they then assaulted the city; Hai Ling led the garrison troops in a desperate two-day defense; the enemy entered the city by scaling ladders and slaughtered bannermen and civilians; Hai Ling and his whole family died as martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: After English troops captured Wusong they entered the Yangzi by sea. In the sixth month they attacked Zhenjiang. Admiral Qi Shen and Liu Chengxiao were defeated and withdrew, then the enemy assaulted the city. Hai Ling led the garrison troops in a desperate two-day defense. The enemy entered the city by scaling ladders and slaughtered bannermen and civilians. Hai Ling and his whole family died as martyrs.

sentences.zh: 予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，諡昭節，入祀昭忠祠，並建祠鎮江，妻及次孫附祀。

translations.literal: He was granted the combined hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry with one additional Junior Commandant of Cavalry, posthumous title Zhaojie, enshrined at the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, and a shrine built at Zhenjiang with his wife and second grandson enshrined together.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the combined hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry with one additional Junior Commandant of Cavalry, the posthumous title Zhaojie, enshrinement at the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, and a shrine built at Zhenjiang with his wife and second grandson enshrined together.

sentences.zh: 當城破時，海齡禁居民不得出，常鎮道周頊棄城走，事後訐海齡妄殺良民，為眾所戕，言官亦論奏，下疆吏究勘得白，詔以闔門死難，大節無虧，仍照都統例賜卹，治頊罪如律。

translations.literal: When the city fell Hai Ling forbade residents to leave; Changzhen Circuit Intendant Zhou Qi abandoned the city and fled; afterward he accused Hai Ling of wantonly killing innocent people and was killed by the crowd; censors also memorialized; the throne ordered frontier officials to investigate and the truth was found; an edict said that because the whole household died in hardship their great integrity was unblemished, posthumous favors were still granted according to the deputy commander precedent, and Zhou Qi was punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Hai Ling forbade residents to leave. Changzhen Circuit Intendant Zhou Qi abandoned the city and fled. Afterward he accused Hai Ling of wantonly killing innocent people and was killed by the crowd. Censors also memorialized. The throne ordered frontier officials to investigate and the truth was found. An edict held that because the whole household died in hardship their great integrity was unblemished, posthumous favors were still granted according to the deputy commander precedent, and Zhou Qi was punished by law.

sentences.zh: 子宜蘭泰，襲世職。

translations.literal: His son Yilantai inherited the hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yilantai inherited the hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: =葛雲飛=葛雲飛，字雨田，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Ge Yunfei, courtesy name Yutian, a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Yunfei, with the courtesy name Yutian, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光三年武進士，授守備，隸浙江水師。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang he passed the military examination and was appointed Garrison Commander, serving in the Zhejiang naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Daoguang reign he passed the military examination and was appointed Garrison Commander, serving in the Zhejiang naval forces.

sentences.zh: 勤於緝捕，常微服巡洋，屢獲劇盜，有名。

translations.literal: Diligent in pursuit and capture, he often patrolled in plain dress and repeatedly seized major bandits, becoming well known.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent in pursuit and capture, he often patrolled in plain dress and repeatedly seized major bandits, becoming well known.

sentences.zh: 洊擢瑞安協副將。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Deputy Commander of the Ruian Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Deputy Commander of the Ruian Brigade.

sentences.zh: 十一年，署定海鎮總兵，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he acted as Commander of Dinghai Garrison and soon received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he served as acting Commander of Dinghai Garrison and soon received substantive appointment.

sentences.zh: 以父憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home on account of his father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 二十年，英兵犯定海，總兵張朝發戰敗失守，巡撫烏爾恭額、提督祝廷彪強起雲飛墨絰從軍，總督鄧廷楨亦薦其可倚，署定海鎮。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year when English troops attacked Dinghai Brigade General Zhang Chaofa was defeated and lost the post; Governor Wu Ergong'e and Admiral Zhu Tingbiao forcibly recalled Yunfei from mourning in hemp to join the army; Governor-General Deng Tingzhen also recommended him as dependable and he acted as Commander of Dinghai Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, when English troops attacked Dinghai, Brigade General Zhang Chaofa was defeated and lost the post. Governor Wu Ergong'e and Admiral Zhu Tingbiao forcibly recalled Yunfei from mourning in hemp to join the army. Governor-General Deng Tingzhen also recommended him as dependable, and he served as acting Commander of Dinghai Garrison.

sentences.zh: 雲飛議先守後戰，扼招寶、金雞兩山，列砲江岸，築土城，集失伍舊兵訓練，軍氣始振。

translations.literal: Yunfei proposed defending first and fighting afterward, holding Zhaobao and Jinjiling hills, lining cannon along the riverbank, building earthen walls, gathering scattered old troops for training, and army morale began to revive.
translations.idiomatic: Yunfei proposed defending first and fighting afterward, holding Zhaobao and Jinjiling hills, lining cannon along the riverbank, building earthen walls, gathering scattered old troops for training, and army morale began to revive.

sentences.zh: 英人安突得出測量形勢，以計擒之，敵始有戒心。

translations.literal: An Englishman named An Tude came out to survey the terrain; Yunfei captured him by stratagem and the enemy first grew wary.
translations.idiomatic: An Englishman named An Tude came out to survey the terrain. Yunfei captured him by stratagem, and the enemy first grew wary.

sentences.zh: 雲飛乘機圖恢復，未果。

translations.literal: Yunfei seized the opportunity to plan recovery but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yunfei seized the opportunity to plan recovery but did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，廣東議款，以香港易定海，欽差大臣伊里布令雲飛率所部渡海收地，然後釋俘，以二鎮帥偕往。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Guangdong negotiated peace, exchanging Hong Kong for Dinghai; Imperial Commissioner Yilibu ordered Yunfei to lead his troops across the sea to recover the territory and then release prisoners, with two brigade commanders to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Guangdong negotiated peace, exchanging Hong Kong for Dinghai. Imperial Commissioner Yilibu ordered Yunfei to lead his troops across the sea to recover the territory and then release prisoners, with two brigade commanders to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 二鎮者，壽春鎮王錫朋、處州鎮鄭國鴻也。

translations.literal: The two commanders were Wang Xipeng of Shouchun Garrison and Zheng Guohong of Chuzhou Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The two commanders were Wang Xipeng of Shouchun Garrison and Zheng Guohong of Chuzhou Garrison.

sentences.zh: 既而裕謙代伊里布，改議戰守，雲飛以定海三面皆山，前臨海無蔽，請於道頭築土城，竹山、曉峰嶺增砲台，而道頭南五奎山、吉祥門、毛港悉置防為犄角。

translations.literal: Then Yu Qian replaced Yilibu and changed policy to war and defense; Yunfei said Dinghai was surrounded by mountains on three sides with no cover before the sea, and requested an earthen wall at Daotou, batteries added at Zhushan and Xiaofeng Ridge, while Wukui Hill, Jixiang Gate, and Maogang to the south of Daotou should all be garrisoned as flank positions.
translations.idiomatic: Then Yu Qian replaced Yilibu and changed policy to war and defense. Yunfei said Dinghai was surrounded by mountains on three sides with no cover before the sea, and requested an earthen wall at Daotou, batteries added at Zhushan and Xiaofeng Ridge, while Wukui Hill, Jixiang Gate, and Maogang to the south of Daotou should all be garrisoned as flank positions.

sentences.zh: 裕謙以費鉅未盡許，則請借三年廉俸興築，益忤裕謙。

translations.literal: Yu Qian did not fully approve because of the great expense; Yunfei then requested to borrow three years' official salary to build, which further offended Yu Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian did not fully approve because of the great expense. Yunfei then requested to borrow three years' official salary to build, which further offended Yu Qian.

sentences.zh: 尋至定海，見雲飛青布帕首、短衣草履，奔走烈日中；

translations.literal: Soon he reached Dinghai and saw Yunfei with a blue cloth wrapped around his head, short coat and straw sandals, running in the blazing sun;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he reached Dinghai and saw Yunfei with a blue cloth wrapped around his head, wearing a short coat and straw sandals, running in the blazing sun;

sentences.zh: 又聞其巡洋捕盜傷臂，奪盜刃刺之，始服其忠勇。

translations.literal: He also heard that while patrolling to capture pirates Yunfei injured his arm; pirates seized a blade to stab him, and only then did he acknowledge his loyal valor.
translations.idiomatic: He also heard that while patrolling to capture pirates Yunfei injured his arm when pirates seized a blade to stab him, and only then did he acknowledge his loyal valor.

sentences.zh: 迨英兵復來犯，砲擊敵艦於竹山門、東港浦，迭卻之，加提督銜。

translations.literal: When English troops again came to attack he fired on enemy ships at Zhushan Gate and Donggangpu and repeatedly drove them back; he was given the rank of provincial admiral.
translations.idiomatic: When English troops again attacked he fired on enemy ships at Zhushan Gate and Donggangpu and repeatedly drove them back, and was given the rank of provincial admiral.

sentences.zh: 於是雲飛屯道頭土城，錫朋、國鴻分防曉峰、竹山。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yunfei garrisoned the earthen wall at Daotou while Xipeng and Guohong divided defense of Xiaofeng and Zhushan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yunfei garrisoned the earthen wall at Daotou while Xipeng and Guohong divided the defense of Xiaofeng and Zhushan.

sentences.zh: 雲飛獨當敵衝，敵連檣進突，登五奎山，砲擊紅衣夷目，乃退。

translations.literal: Yunfei alone bore the enemy's main thrust; the enemy advanced in a line of connected ships and stormed Wukui Hill; cannon fire struck a red-coated English officer and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yunfei alone bore the enemy's main thrust. The enemy advanced in a line of connected ships and stormed Wukui Hill. Cannon fire struck a red-coated English officer and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 次日，敵蔽山後發砲仰擊，亦隔山應之。

translations.literal: The next day the enemy concealed themselves behind the hill and fired upward; Yunfei also replied from across the hill.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the enemy concealed themselves behind the hill and fired upward, and Yunfei replied from across the hill.

sentences.zh: 夜，敵乘霧至，直逼土城，砲中載藥敵船，轟殲甚眾。

translations.literal: At night the enemy came in fog and pressed straight to the earthen wall; cannon struck an enemy ship loaded with powder and very many were blasted to destruction.
translations.idiomatic: At night the enemy came in fog and pressed straight to the earthen wall. Cannon struck an enemy ship loaded with powder and very many were blasted to destruction.

sentences.zh: 越日，乃肉搏來奪曉峰嶺，分攻竹山門，錫朋、國鴻皆戰歿，縣城遂陷。
